author: RYAN SPOEHR
title: Traffic accident occurs during ICE investigation in Janesville - NewsBreak
text:
By RYAN SPOEHR ,
15 hours ago
JANESVILLE — Officials say two vehicles crashed during a federal operation with multiple agencies that included the Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency Wednesday, according to the Janesville Police Department.
In a statement late Wednesday, the police department said the crash happened during “targeted operations” by multiple federal agencies that the department was “not asked to assist in, participate in, or provide information for.”
In the statement, the police department directed inquiries regarding “detention or action taken as a part of the federal investigation” to the ICE Chicago Field Office.
A federal vehicle and a van collided just before 7 a.m., but the police department still does not know which vehicle initiated the contact, Chief Chad Pearson said. The Janesville PD is also still investigating how many federal agents were involved in the crash. Pearson was able to confirm there was a driver in the federal vehicle, but did not know if there were any passengers.
The operation itself started at 5:30 a.m, Pearson told The Gazette. He said the department was notified at about 12:30 p.m. that it had concluded.
In a statement on social media, Pearson described the van as a “transport van” and in an interview with The Gazette said it was a “personal van.” The van was driven by the individual that federal law enforcement was targeting.
However, there was not a pursuit at the time of the crash. Some damage was caused to the vehicles, but they were not traveling at high rates of speed, Pearson said.
“The tactics that were employed in regards to how they made contact with that individual, we don’t know,” Pearson said.
The incident came a day after ICE made arrests in Beloit.
The Gazette made five phone calls Wednesday afternoon to a phone number the Chicago ICE field office line states is a media contact. Each time, a reporter was greeted immediately with a busy signal. The Gazette also sent a request to a media email to ask if there were any arrests and how many agents were involved in the crash with no response.
Adams MultiMedia was also treated to a prerecorded message the previous day from the Madison field office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation — when directed to reach out to that office for information on the operation in Beloit.
